variables: any identifier declared in an Inputs:/Input:/Variables:/Variable:/Vars:/Var: block (letters, digits, underscore, period; cannot start with digit or period; case-insensitive)
labels inside Buy("...")/Sell("...")/from entry("...") are strings, not identifiers

notes: TOKENIZER: case-insensitive identifiers; comments are `//` to end of line and `{ ... }` block (non-nesting — the FIRST `}` ends it, so a brace inside a header comment is a compile error; lint should flag any `{` inside an open block comment); strings are double-quoted only ("..."), no escape sequences documented; statement terminator `;`; attributes are bracketed `[Name = value]` at file top; bar offset `[n]` after an identifier or call; operators `= <> < > <= >= + - * / ( )` plus `and or not`; numeric literals may be `0900` (leading zeros, HHmm times) and decimals `0.8`/`.8`. Keyword phrases are multi-token (`next bar at market`, `this bar on close`, `crosses over`, `from entry`, `sell short`, `buy to cover`): the linter should match tokens individually — each token is in `keywords`. `keywords` = MC reserved words/skip words a signal may legitimately use (lowercased); `functions` = built-in study functions from the shipped EL-compatible library (average/averagefc/highest/lowest/rsi seen in MC's own docs and built-in signals; the rest from the TS reference and assumed shipped — treat a miss as WARN, not ERROR); `variables` describes implicit names and the declaration rule, not a fixed list — the linter must collect declared Inputs/Variables from the source. `unsupported` = ERROR: OOEL (method/using/elsystem/vector/dictionary/...), MC.NET (Orders.*, Bars.*, CalcBar), Pine (strategy.*, ta.*, @version), and TS-only words MC listed as not supported in 2008 that still have no page in the MC keyword categories; SetExitOnClose is listed because MC documents it as backtest-only and asks for the EndOfDayExit signal instead — flag as ERROR so the agent rewrites to a Time-based exit. `discouraged` = WARN only: `once` compiles in MC (forum-confirmed, no wiki page) but templates use `CurrentBar = 1`; `this bar on close` only for exec_at_close bars; `[IntrabarOrderGeneration = true]` changes `next bar` to next tick; `repeat/until` has parenthesis quirks (MC 9); `plot` is numeric-only and pointless in a signal. UNVERIFIED items: exact membership of `functions` beyond those named above; whether MC still lacks every 2008-list word (the 2008 list dropped setbreakeven/setdollartrailing/setpercenttrailing/i_marketposition etc., which are now documented — those are in `keywords`). NAME CLASH: an Input/Variable declared with a name in `keywords` (e.g. Contracts, Range, Text, Data, Total, Entry, Short, Cover, All) is an ERROR — reserved words cannot be declared.
